metaDescription: Boxer vaccine schedule with core ages in weeks. Set reminders so Boxer boosters are not missed.

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: Plan Boxer social milestones around the schedule rows, not the other way around, because the 16-week finish is the usual green light clinics cite for broader Boxer exposure.
Weight range 50-80 lb (23-36 kg) and grooming needs (Weekly brush; wipe facial folds.) belong in the same Boxer household ops list as vaccine dates when busy weeks collide.
If your Boxer is also monitored for cardiomyopathy / arrhythmia screening, ask whether bloodwork or orthopedic checks can share a visit with a booster to cut missed Boxer appointments.
After the Boxer puppy/kitten series, keep adult DA2PP / DHPP and rabies renewals on 7/3/1-day reminders so year-two surprises disappear.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Delayed Boxer boosters usually need one well-timed catch-up, not a homemade double dose, because spacing rules protect the puppy and guilt math does not.
Bring prior dates for every Boxer row (8, 12, 16, 16 weeks on this page’s plan) so clinics can decide whether an extra DA2PP / DHPP booster is required based on gap length and age.
If rabies was the missed Boxer item, legal and boarding consequences stack on top of medical ones — restore compliance before the next Boxer kennel reservation.
PetClues should hold both the new Boxer due date and the certificate photo so household members stop arguing about which fridge sticky note is current.

faqs.question: When does the Boxer core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Boxer misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read Boxer health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the Boxer adult health guide for breed predispositions such as cancer risk (breed-associated), then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
